title: AlexNet wins ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012)
summary: A GPU-trained deep convolutional network from Hinton's Toronto lab won ILSVRC 2012 with 15.3% top-5 error versus 26.2% for the runner-up.
significance: Interpretation: Converted the field to deep learning on GPUs almost overnight and tied AI progress to commodity NVIDIA hardware plus large labeled datasets.

title: word2vec dense word embeddings
summary: Mikolov et al. at Google released word2vec, efficiently learning vector word representations from large unlabeled corpora.
significance: Interpretation: Made 'learn representations from raw text' the default in NLP, a precursor of self-supervised pretraining.

title: DeepMind DQN learns Atari from pixels
summary: DeepMind's Deep Q-Network learned many Atari games from raw pixels using one architecture.
significance: Interpretation: Made deep reinforcement learning the leading candidate path to general agents for the rest of the decade.

title: Google acquires DeepMind
summary: Google agreed to acquire London-based DeepMind; the price was not disclosed and press reports ranged roughly $400-650M. It followed Google's 2013 purchase of Hinton's DNNresearch and Facebook's creation of FAIR under LeCun (Dec 2013).
significance: Interpretation: First large bet on an explicitly AGI-oriented lab; set the pattern of hyperscalers owning or funding frontier labs.

title: Generative adversarial networks
summary: Goodfellow et al. introduced GANs, training a generator against a discriminator.
significance: Interpretation: Opened modern generative modeling of images; the generative lineage later passed to diffusion models in 2021-22.

title: Bostrom's 'Superintelligence' frames AI existential risk
summary: Nick Bostrom published Superintelligence, arguing advanced AI could pose an existential risk.
significance: Interpretation: Gave a then-fringe risk concern an academic vocabulary that influenced OpenAI's founders and, later, the 2023 statements on extinction risk.

title: Sequence-to-sequence learning and attention
summary: Sutskever, Vinyals and Le published LSTM encoder-decoder translation; Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio introduced attention the same month.
significance: Interpretation: Established end-to-end neural language generation; attention became the core of the Transformer three years later.

title: Google open-sources TensorFlow
summary: Google released TensorFlow as open source on 9 November 2015.
significance: Interpretation: Treated frameworks as strategic distribution for cloud and talent; frameworks then commoditized (PyTorch overtook TensorFlow in research).

title: ResNet surpasses estimated human ImageNet error
summary: Microsoft Research's 152-layer residual networks won ILSVRC 2015 with 3.57% top-5 error.
significance: Interpretation: Residual connections made very deep networks trainable and became a component of the Transformer; vision benchmarks began to saturate.

title: OpenAI founded as non-profit with $1B pledged
summary: OpenAI launched as a non-profit research company with $1 billion in total commitments from Altman, Musk, Brockman, Thiel, Hoffman, AWS, Infosys and others.
significance: Interpretation: Created a lab explicitly aimed at AGI outside big tech; its later scaling bet and capital structure reshaped the industry.

title: AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol 4-1
summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4-1 in Seoul in March 2016, years before many experts expected Go to fall.
significance: Interpretation: A public 'Sputnik moment', especially in China and Korea, that raised AI to a national-strategy priority.

title: NVIDIA Pascal P100 and DGX-1; first DGX-1 to OpenAI
summary: NVIDIA launched the P100 and DGX-1 system for deep learning; Jensen Huang delivered the first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016.
significance: Interpretation: NVIDIA repositioned from gaming to deep-learning systems; its FY2017 filing attributed 145% datacenter growth to deep learning training.

title: Google discloses the TPU
summary: Google revealed it had used custom Tensor Processing Units for inference in its data centers for over a year.
significance: Interpretation: First evidence that hyperscalers would design their own AI silicon; the TPU line later trained PaLM and Gemini.

title: DeepMind ML cuts Google data-center cooling energy by up to 40%
summary: DeepMind reported its system reduced energy used for cooling in Google data centers by up to 40%.
significance: Interpretation: Energy entered the AI story as an application area, not yet as a binding constraint on AI itself.

title: NVIDIA Volta V100 with Tensor Cores
summary: NVIDIA introduced the Volta V100 with Tensor Cores; it began shipping in the first half of NVIDIA fiscal 2018 and drove datacenter revenue to $1.93B, up 133%.
significance: Interpretation: Dedicated matrix-math units made GPUs AI-specific accelerators, widening NVIDIA's lead over CPUs.

title: Google declares an 'AI-first' strategy at I/O
summary: Sundar Pichai described Google's shift from mobile-first to AI-first and announced Cloud TPUs.
significance: Interpretation: Defined the period's belief that incumbents with users and data would capture AI value by embedding it in existing products.

title: 'Attention Is All You Need': the Transformer
summary: Google researchers introduced the Transformer, built entirely on attention.
significance: Interpretation: Its parallelizable architecture made scaling on GPUs/TPUs efficient and became the substrate of every later foundation model.

title: China's New Generation AI Development Plan
summary: China's State Council set a goal of world leadership in AI by 2030 with a core industry over 1 trillion yuan.
significance: Interpretation: Turned AI into an explicit US-China strategic competition, foreshadowing chip export controls.

title: AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero: superhuman play from self-play
summary: AlphaGo Zero (Oct 2017) learned Go without human data; AlphaZero (Dec 2017) generalized to chess and shogi. AlphaGo Zero remained the largest training run by compute until August 2021 (Epoch).
significance: Interpretation: Reinforced the belief that RL plus search, not language modeling, was the frontier path; RL returned in 2024-25 inside LLM reasoning.

title: OpenAI 'AI and Compute': 3.4-month doubling
summary: OpenAI estimated compute in the largest training runs had grown more than 300,000x since 2012, doubling every 3.4 months.
significance: Interpretation: Reframed AI progress as a compute-supply story, the intellectual basis for OpenAI's capital-raising strategy.

title: Pretrain-then-fine-tune: ELMo, GPT-1, BERT
summary: ELMo (Feb 2018), OpenAI's GPT-1 (Jun 2018) and Google's BERT (Oct 2018) showed self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled text transfers to many tasks.
significance: Interpretation: Made language-model pretraining the NLP default; BERT was the consensus winner, while GPT's generative decoder approach was the minority that later dominated.

title: GPT-2 and staged release
summary: OpenAI announced the 1.5B-parameter GPT-2 and initially withheld the full weights over misuse concerns, releasing it in stages through November 2019.
significance: Interpretation: First time a lab treated a language model's capability as a release-policy question; previewed later open vs closed debates.

title: OpenAI LP 'capped-profit' structure
summary: OpenAI created a capped-profit company governed by its non-profit, capping first-round returns at 100x.
significance: Interpretation: Acknowledged that frontier AI needs billions in capital; the hybrid governance later produced the November 2023 board crisis.

title: NVIDIA agrees to buy Mellanox for $6.9B
summary: NVIDIA agreed to acquire interconnect maker Mellanox; it closed in April 2020 and contributed 10% of NVIDIA revenue in FY2021.
significance: Interpretation: Extended NVIDIA from chips to data-center systems; networking became part of its moat in the cluster era.

title: Sutton's 'The Bitter Lesson'
summary: Richard Sutton argued that general methods leveraging computation ultimately beat human-knowledge-based approaches.
significance: Interpretation: Became the canonical statement of the scaling worldview, still a minority position in academia at the time.

title: US adds Huawei to the Entity List
summary: The US Commerce Department restricted Huawei's access to US-origin technology.
significance: Interpretation: Started using semiconductor supply chains as a geopolitical weapon, the template for the 2022 AI chip controls.

title: Strubell et al. quantify energy cost of NLP training
summary: An ACL 2019 paper estimated the energy and carbon costs of training large NLP models.
significance: Interpretation: First widely cited warning that AI's energy footprint mattered, though at 2019 scale it was framed as an environmental concern, not a capacity constraint.

title: Microsoft invests $1B in OpenAI
summary: Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI, with Azure as exclusive cloud provider.
significance: Interpretation: Created the hyperscaler-lab coupling (compute for equity and exclusivity) that defined frontier AI economics afterwards.

title: Kaplan et al. 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models'
summary: OpenAI showed language-model loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute over more than seven orders of magnitude.
significance: Interpretation: Made capability gains predictable enough to justify large capital commitments; its parameter-heavy recipe was revised by Chinchilla in 2022.

title: Microsoft's Azure supercomputer for OpenAI
summary: Microsoft said it built for OpenAI one of the world's top five supercomputers with 285,000+ CPU cores and 10,000 GPUs. The same month NVIDIA launched the A100.
significance: Interpretation: Bespoke hyperscaler clusters for one lab became the unit of frontier competition.

title: GPT-3 and the OpenAI API
summary: OpenAI published GPT-3 (175B parameters, ~3.14e23 FLOP) showing few-shot in-context learning, and opened a commercial API in June 2020. Microsoft took an exclusive license to GPT-3 in September 2020.
significance: Interpretation: Demonstrated that one general model could be prompted for many tasks, and introduced model-as-API as a business.

title: AlphaFold 2 at CASP14
summary: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 reached a median GDT of ~92.4 at CASP14, competitive with experimental structure determination for many proteins.
significance: Interpretation: Strongest evidence yet of AI producing scientific value; recognized with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (hindsight).

title: Global semiconductor shortage
summary: Pandemic demand shifts and supply disruptions produced a chip shortage that cut auto production through 2021.
significance: Interpretation: Made semiconductor supply chains a political issue, feeding the CHIPS Act; AI-specific supply limits (CoWoS, HBM) arrived later.

title: European Commission proposes the AI Act
summary: The Commission proposed a risk-based regulation for AI systems.
significance: Interpretation: Its pre-LLM, use-case-based design had to be retrofitted for general-purpose models in 2023.

title: Anthropic founded ($124M Series A)
summary: Former OpenAI researchers including Dario and Daniela Amodei announced Anthropic with a $124M Series A.
significance: Interpretation: Institutionalized 'safety-focused scaling' and created a third frontier lab later backed by Amazon and Google.

title: GitHub Copilot technical preview
summary: GitHub launched a Copilot preview powered by OpenAI Codex; general availability followed June 2022 at $10/month.
significance: Interpretation: First mass-market paid LLM product, showing coding as the first high-value use case and incumbents' distribution advantage.

title: 'On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models'
summary: Stanford CRFM coined 'foundation models' for broadly trained models adaptable to many tasks.
significance: Interpretation: Gave academia and policymakers a shared frame; the term later entered the EU AI Act and US EO.

title: Chain-of-thought prompting
summary: Wei et al. showed prompting large models with intermediate reasoning steps sharply improved reasoning performance.
significance: Interpretation: First evidence that spending more inference tokens on reasoning raises capability, the seed of 2024-25 reasoning models.

title: NVIDIA announces H100 (Hopper)
summary: NVIDIA announced the H100 with a Transformer Engine supporting FP8.
significance: Interpretation: The chip of the generative-AI boom; demand for it in 2023 far exceeded supply.

title: InstructGPT: RLHF makes small models preferred over GPT-3
summary: OpenAI showed outputs of a 1.3B RLHF-tuned model were preferred over 175B GPT-3.
significance: Interpretation: Post-training, not only pretraining scale, became a key lever for usefulness.

title: Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling
summary: DeepMind's 70B Chinchilla, trained on 1.4T tokens with Gopher's compute, outperformed Gopher (280B) and GPT-3.
significance: Interpretation: Shifted the bottleneck from parameters to training data and made smaller, cheaper-to-serve models the target.

title: PaLM 540B on Pathways/TPU v4
summary: Google trained the 540B dense PaLM on 6,144 TPU v4 chips (~2.56e24 FLOP).
significance: Interpretation: Showed Google's vertically integrated TPU stack was competitive at the frontier.

title: Diffusion image generation goes public: DALL-E 2, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion
summary: DALL-E 2 (April), Midjourney's open beta (July) and the openly licensed Stable Diffusion weights (22 Aug 2022) brought text-to-image generation to the public. They built on CLIP/DALL-E (Jan 2021) and open datasets such as LAION-5B.
significance: Interpretation: First consumer generative-AI wave and first proof open weights could spread a capability overnight; 'generative AI' became an investment category before ChatGPT.

title: CHIPS and Science Act
summary: The US enacted roughly $52.7B in semiconductor support including ~$39B in manufacturing incentives.
significance: Interpretation: Industrial policy aimed at physical supply-chain resilience, a precursor to treating AI infrastructure as national infrastructure.

title: US export controls on advanced AI chips to China
summary: BIS restricted exports to China of A100/H100-class AI chips and advanced chipmaking equipment.
significance: Interpretation: Made compute access an instrument of state power and split the AI hardware market geographically.

title: ChatGPT launches
summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, fine-tuned from GPT-3.5 with RLHF, as a free research preview on 30 Nov 2022; UBS estimated 100M monthly users by January 2023.
significance: Interpretation: Turned LLMs from a developer API into a mass consumer product and triggered the capital and policy response of 2023.

title: Microsoft's multibillion investment in OpenAI
summary: Microsoft announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment in OpenAI, widely reported as $10B.
significance: Interpretation: Set the template of hyperscaler capital in exchange for compute consumption and model rights.

title: Microsoft launches GPT-powered Bing
summary: Microsoft launched Bing chat on a next-generation OpenAI model (later confirmed as GPT-4).
significance: Interpretation: Opened the incumbent-distribution battle over search; Google's search share proved more resilient than expected (hindsight).

title: Meta LLaMA released and weights leak
summary: Meta released LLaMA (7B-65B) under a research license; LLaMA-13B outperformed GPT-3 on most benchmarks; weights leaked publicly in early March.
significance: Interpretation: Launched the open-weight ecosystem; capability at a given size became reproducible and commoditizing.

title: GPT-4
summary: OpenAI announced GPT-4 on 14 March 2023, with near-human results on many professional exams and no disclosure of size, compute or data; Epoch estimates ~2e25 FLOP.
significance: Interpretation: Set the frontier benchmark that competitors took most of 2023 to approach; ended routine disclosure of training details.

title: CAIS one-sentence statement on extinction risk
summary: Hundreds of researchers and lab leaders signed a statement that mitigating AI extinction risk should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. It followed the FLI 'pause' letter (22 Mar 2023) and Geoffrey Hinton's departure from Google to speak about AI risk (1 May 2023).
significance: Interpretation: Lab CEOs publicly endorsing extinction-risk framing helped set up the Bletchley summit and the EO.

title: Llama 2 open weights for commercial use
summary: Meta released Llama 2 (7B-70B) with chat variants, free for most commercial use, with Microsoft as preferred partner.
significance: Interpretation: Legitimized open weights as a corporate strategy (commoditize the complement).

title: NVIDIA data-center revenue doubles in a quarter amid H100 shortage
summary: NVIDIA reported $10.32B quarterly data-center revenue, more than double the prior quarter, with H100 supply constrained; FY2024 data-center revenue reached $47.5B, up 217%. NVIDIA had briefly passed a $1T market value on 30 May 2023.
significance: Interpretation: The ChatGPT demand shock showed up first and most clearly in GPU revenue.

title: Amazon to invest up to $4B in Anthropic
summary: Amazon agreed to invest up to $4B in Anthropic, with AWS as primary cloud and use of Trainium/Inferentia chips.
significance: Interpretation: Every hyperscaler now had a frontier-lab partner; custom silicon was part of the deal.

title: US Executive Order 14110 on AI
summary: The order required developers of models trained above 1e26 operations to report training and red-teaming to the government.
significance: Interpretation: First US rule keyed to training compute, treating FLOP as a regulatory proxy for risk; revoked in January 2025 (hindsight).

title: Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit
summary: 28 countries plus the EU, including the US and China, signed the Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI risks on 1-2 Nov 2023.
significance: Interpretation: First intergovernmental agreement on frontier AI risk; spawned national AI safety institutes.

title: OpenAI DevDay: GPT-4 Turbo price cut, GPTs, Assistants API
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-4 Turbo at $10/$30 per 1M input/output tokens (a third and a half of GPT-4's launch prices) plus custom GPTs and an Assistants API.
significance: Interpretation: Price per capability began falling fast; OpenAI tried to become a platform rather than only a model vendor.

title: OpenAI board fires and reinstates Sam Altman
summary: OpenAI's non-profit board removed Altman on 17 Nov 2023; after a staff revolt and Microsoft's offer to hire them, he returned with a new board on 21-22 Nov.
significance: Interpretation: Showed that capital, compute partners and talent outweighed non-profit governance at frontier labs.

title: Google launches Gemini 1.0
summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 1.0 (Ultra, Pro, Nano), natively multimodal and trained on TPUs.
significance: Interpretation: Google's first credible GPT-4-class response; signalled the frontier would be a multi-player race.

title: EU AI Act political agreement
summary: EU co-legislators reached a provisional agreement on the AI Act, adding obligations for general-purpose AI models.
significance: Interpretation: First comprehensive binding AI law, retrofitted for foundation models.

title: Mistral's Mixtral 8x7B open sparse MoE
summary: Mistral released Mixtral 8x7B under Apache 2.0, a sparse mixture-of-experts using ~13B of ~47B parameters per token, matching or beating GPT-3.5 on many benchmarks.
significance: Interpretation: Brought MoE into the open-weight mainstream and showed GPT-3.5-class quality had become cheap and widely available.

title: New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft
summary: The NYT filed a copyright suit alleging unlicensed use of its articles for model training.
significance: Interpretation: Turned training-data provenance into a legal and commercial bottleneck, pushing labs toward data licensing.

title: Gemini 1.5 Pro ships 1M-token context
summary: Google previewed Gemini 1.5 Pro, a mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context window.
significance: Interpretation: made long context a competitive axis and weakened the assumption that retrieval pipelines were the only way to ground models in large corpora.

title: OpenAI previews Sora text-to-video
summary: OpenAI previewed Sora, a diffusion-transformer video model producing minute-long clips; public release came in December 2024.
significance: Interpretation: extended the 'scale the transformer' thesis to video and fed the 'world simulator' framing.

title: Claude 3 family ends GPT-4's solo lead
summary: Anthropic released Claude 3 (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet on 2024-06-20.
significance: Interpretation: the frontier became a multi-lab race, undercutting the belief that a single lab's lead was durable.

title: License-and-hire deals absorb Inflection and Character.AI
summary: Microsoft hired Inflection's leadership with a ~$650M licensing payment (Mar 2024); Google did a ~$2.7B license-and-rehire of Character.AI's founders (Aug 2024).
significance: Interpretation: signalled that independent second-tier model labs struggled to fund frontier training and that talent, not companies, was the asset being bought.

title: Amazon buys nuclear-adjacent data center campus from Talen
summary: Amazon acquired Talen Energy's data center campus next to the Susquehanna nuclear plant (~$650M).
significance: Interpretation: first clear sign that hyperscalers would co-locate with firm (nuclear) generation to secure AI power.

title: GPT-4o: native multimodal flagship made free
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-4o, a natively multimodal model, free in ChatGPT and at half GPT-4 Turbo's API price.
significance: Interpretation: GPT-4-class capability became a free consumer commodity, shifting competition to distribution and price.

title: 'Situational Awareness' essay frames AGI-by-2027 and a compute race
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner published a long essay extrapolating compute OOMs to AGI around 2027 and trillion-dollar clusters.
significance: Interpretation: crystallized the national-security and compute-scaling narrative later echoed in Stargate and US policy.

title: Sequoia's 'AI's $600B Question'
summary: David Cahn estimated a ~$600B gap between implied AI infrastructure spend and AI revenue.
significance: Interpretation: became the canonical framing of the AI-bubble debate for the next two years.

title: Nvidia briefly becomes the world's most valuable company
summary: Nvidia's market cap passed ~$3.3T, briefly overtaking Microsoft.
significance: Interpretation: markets priced accelerators as the main value-capture layer of the AI stack.

title: Llama 3.1 405B: frontier-class open weights
summary: Meta released Llama 3.1 405B open weights alongside Zuckerberg's 'Open Source AI Is the Path Forward'; Llama 3 8B/70B had shipped in April.
significance: Interpretation: open weights near the frontier challenged the idea that model weights themselves were the moat.

title: GPT-4o mini prices GPT-4-class quality at $0.15/1M input tokens
summary: OpenAI released GPT-4o mini at $0.15/$0.60 per 1M input/output tokens, versus $30/$60 for GPT-4 at launch in March 2023.
significance: Interpretation: made 'LLMflation' (rapid constant-capability price decline) visible to every developer.

title: EU AI Act enters into force
summary: The AI Act entered into force with staged application dates for prohibitions (Feb 2025), GPAI duties (Aug 2025) and high-risk rules (Aug 2026, later delayed).
significance: Interpretation: first comprehensive horizontal AI law; set the compliance baseline that later became a target for simplification.

title: OpenAI o1: inference-time compute becomes a scaling axis
summary: OpenAI released o1-preview, trained with RL to reason in long chains of thought, with performance scaling in both RL training and test-time compute.
significance: Interpretation: reframed scaling from pretraining-only to RL plus test-time compute, shifting demand toward inference and opening the reasoning era.

title: xAI Colossus: ~100k H100s online in Memphis
summary: xAI announced its ~100,000-GPU Colossus cluster online after about four months of construction.
significance: Interpretation: showed that speed-to-power and build execution could be a competitive advantage in its own right.

title: Nuclear PPAs: Microsoft restarts TMI Unit 1; Google signs Kairos SMRs
summary: Constellation and Microsoft signed a 20-year PPA to restart TMI Unit 1 (Sept 20); Google agreed to buy up to ~500 MW from Kairos SMRs (Oct 14, 2024).
significance: Interpretation: AI demand began reviving retired firm generation and underwriting next-generation nuclear, making power a recognized binding constraint.

title: California Gov. Newsom vetoes SB 1047
summary: Newsom vetoed the frontier-model safety bill, citing its focus on model size rather than deployment risk.
significance: Interpretation: marked the limit of compute-threshold safety regulation in the US and shifted fights to transparency laws and federal preemption.

title: Nobel prizes to Hinton (Physics) and Hassabis/Jumper (Chemistry)
summary: Physics 2024 went to Hopfield and Hinton; Chemistry 2024 half to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold.
significance: Interpretation: institutional scientific validation of deep learning and of AI-for-science.

title: Computer use (Oct) and Model Context Protocol (Nov) from Anthropic
summary: Anthropic shipped computer-use beta (Oct 22, 2024) and open-sourced MCP (Nov 25, 2024), later adopted by OpenAI (Mar 2025) and others.
significance: Interpretation: MCP became the de facto tool-connection standard, commoditizing integration and accelerating agents.

title: LBNL: data centers 4.4% of US electricity, up to 12% by 2028
summary: DOE/LBNL reported data centers used ~176 TWh (4.4%) of US electricity in 2023 and could reach 6.7-12% by 2028.
significance: Interpretation: gave policymakers an official baseline for AI-driven load growth.

title: o3 scores ~76-88% on ARC-AGI-1
summary: OpenAI previewed o3; ARC Prize verified ~75.7% (limited compute) and ~87.5% (high compute) on ARC-AGI-1.
significance: Interpretation: test-time compute cracked a benchmark designed to resist scaling, though at very high cost per task.

title: DeepSeek-R1: open-weight reasoning at a fraction of the cost
summary: DeepSeek released R1 under MIT license, matching o1 on many benchmarks; its V3 base reported a ~$5.6M final training run.
significance: Interpretation: showed RL-based reasoning could be replicated cheaply and openly, compressing frontier leads and triggering a market repricing.

title: Stargate: $500B US AI infrastructure pledge
summary: OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX announced Stargate, intending $500B over four years ($100B immediately).
significance: Interpretation: moved frontier labs from renting compute to directly sponsoring GW-scale campuses.

title: Nvidia loses ~$589B in one day
summary: Nvidia fell ~17% after DeepSeek, the largest single-day market-value loss for a US company at the time.
significance: Interpretation: markets briefly feared efficiency would shrink compute demand (Jevons debate); demand subsequently accelerated.

title: Claude Code launches; coding agents become the killer app
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Code with Claude 3.7 Sonnet (preview) and made it GA with Claude 4 (May 22, 2025).
significance: Interpretation: terminal-native coding agents became the first agent category with large paid usage, reshaping revenue mix toward agentic tokens.

title: METR: AI task horizons double every ~7 months
summary: METR found frontier models' 50% task-completion horizon had doubled ~every 7 months since 2019 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet ~50 minutes).
significance: Interpretation: offered a single trend line for agent capability that anchored forecasts and policy discussion.

title: Reasoning goes mainstream: Gemini 2.5 Pro, o3, o4-mini
summary: Google shipped Gemini 2.5 Pro (Mar 25) as a thinking model; OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini (Apr 16) with tool use inside reasoning.
significance: Interpretation: reasoning became table stakes across labs and inference-time compute a standard cost driver.

title: H20 export licensing and the revenue-share reversal
summary: The US required licenses for Nvidia H20 sales to China (Apr 2025), then allowed them under a 15% revenue-share arrangement (Aug 2025); H200 sales were later allowed under license.
significance: Interpretation: chip export policy turned transactional, and China accelerated domestic accelerators and open models.

title: Claude 4 (Opus/Sonnet) targets long-running agents
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, emphasizing multi-hour agentic coding; activated ASL-3 protections for Opus 4.
significance: Interpretation: frontier competition shifted from chat quality to sustained agentic work.

title: Meta buys 49% of Scale AI and forms Superintelligence Labs
summary: Meta invested ~$14.3B in Scale AI, hired Alexandr Wang, and launched Meta Superintelligence Labs with large talent offers.
significance: Interpretation: talent and data pipelines priced like strategic assets; marked Meta's pivot away from Llama-first open strategy.

title: Chinese open-weight wave: Qwen3, Kimi K2, DeepSeek V3.x
summary: Alibaba (Qwen3, Apr), Moonshot (Kimi K2, Jul) and DeepSeek (V3.1/V3.2) released strong open-weight models.
significance: Interpretation: China became the center of gravity for open weights as Meta retreated, keeping the open-closed gap to a few months.

title: US AI Action Plan
summary: The White House issued America's AI Action Plan prioritizing deregulation, data-center/power permitting and AI exports.
significance: Interpretation: US policy pivoted from safety framing (2023 EO) to build-out and competitiveness.

title: GPT-5 launches to mixed reception
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 as a routed system at $1.25/$10 per 1M tokens.
significance: Interpretation: aggressive pricing and an incremental-feeling launch fed 'scaling plateau' and bubble narratives in late 2025.

title: MIT NANDA '95% of GenAI pilots fail' report
summary: MIT NANDA's 'GenAI Divide' report claimed ~95% of organizations saw zero measurable return from GenAI pilots.
significance: Interpretation: became a widely cited (and contested) data point in the enterprise-ROI and bubble debate.

title: Stanford 'Canaries in the Coal Mine' entry-level labor study
summary: ADP payroll analysis found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed occupations.
significance: Interpretation: first large-sample evidence of early-career labor effects, shifting the labor debate from speculation to measurement.

title: OpenAI's GW-scale compute deals with Oracle, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom
summary: Reported ~$300B Oracle contract, Nvidia up-to-$100B investment LOI (10 GW), AMD 6 GW with warrants, Broadcom 10 GW, AWS $38B.
significance: Interpretation: supplier-financed demand ('circular financing') became the core of the bubble critique.

title: OpenAI recapitalizes as a public benefit corporation
summary: OpenAI's for-profit became OpenAI Group PBC under the OpenAI Foundation; Microsoft took ~27%.
significance: Interpretation: removed the structural barrier to mega-fundraising and an eventual IPO.

title: Nvidia first company to reach $5 trillion market cap
summary: Nvidia closed above $5T market capitalization.
significance: Interpretation: peak expression of the belief that value accrues to the accelerator layer.

title: Gemini 3 retakes benchmark lead; Antigravity agent IDE
summary: Google released Gemini 3 across Search, the Gemini app and developer platforms with record benchmark claims (e.g., 37.5% HLE).
significance: Interpretation: shifted perception toward Google's full-stack (TPU + distribution) advantage.

title: Oracle CDS at highest since 2009 as AI debt fears mount
summary: Oracle five-year CDS hit post-2009 highs amid large bond issuance and ~$248B in data-center lease commitments.
significance: Interpretation: AI-bubble concern moved from equity valuations to credit markets.

title: Executive Order 14365 targets state AI laws
summary: Trump signed an EO creating a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws and directing a federal preemption proposal.
significance: Interpretation: federal-vs-state jurisdiction became the central US AI governance fight.

title: Q1 frontier refresh: Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro
summary: Aggregator timelines list Claude Opus 4.6 (Feb 5) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (Feb 19, 2026).
significance: Interpretation: release cadence compressed to roughly bi-monthly frontier increments.

title: Nvidia FY2026: $215.9B revenue, $62.3B data center quarter
summary: NVIDIA reported Q4 FY2026 revenue $68.1B and data center $62.3B; FY2026 revenue $215.9B (+65%).
significance: Interpretation: demand kept accelerating despite the DeepSeek scare and bubble debate.

title: Pentagon labels Anthropic a supply chain risk
summary: After Anthropic refused to drop restrictions on mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons uses, the Pentagon designated it a supply chain risk.
significance: Interpretation: lab usage policies became a direct point of conflict with the US government.

title: OpenAI raises $122B at $852B post-money
summary: OpenAI reportedly closed a $122B round at an $852B valuation led by SoftBank and Microsoft.
significance: Interpretation: private capital scale for labs reached sovereign-wealth levels.

title: Project Glasswing: Claude Mythos withheld for cyber-defense only
summary: Anthropic gave its unreleased Claude Mythos Preview to 40+ security partners to find and fix vulnerabilities instead of releasing it generally.
significance: Interpretation: first major case of a lab withholding a frontier model on offensive-cyber capability grounds.

title: Meta's first post-Llama model (Avocado series) after delays
summary: After delaying Avocado, Meta reportedly released Muse Spark (first Avocado-series model) in the Meta AI app, replacing Llama in its assistants.
significance: Interpretation: confirmed Meta's shift away from open Llama releases toward closed, product-first models.

title: GPT-5.5 released
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.5, framed as a step toward doing work on a computer.
significance: Interpretation: computer-use agents became the headline capability for frontier releases.

title: DeepSeek V4: 1.6T open MoE with 1M context
summary: DeepSeek released V4-Pro (1.6T) and V4-Flash (284B) open-weight MoE previews with 1M-token context.
significance: Interpretation: Chinese open weights stayed within months of the frontier (Epoch: ~4-month lag in 2026).

title: Big-four 2026 capex guidance reaches ~$700-725B
summary: Q1 2026 earnings put combined Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta 2026 capex at roughly $700-725B, up ~75% from ~$410B in 2025; three of four raised guidance.
significance: Interpretation: capex kept rising despite bubble concerns, with analysts projecting >$1T in 2027; part of the rise is component inflation.

title: Anthropic Series H: $65B at $965B; $47B run-rate
summary: Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation, above OpenAI's $852B, with run-rate revenue above $47B.
significance: Interpretation: enterprise/agentic-coding revenue made Anthropic the highest-valued private lab, overturning the consumer-first assumption.

title: OpenAI confidentially files for an IPO
summary: OpenAI confidentially submitted a draft registration statement (reported May 22/June 8), with reports of a Q4 2026 target at $852B-$1T+.
significance: Interpretation: frontier labs moving to public markets would test AI valuations against disclosure.

title: US Commerce order leads Anthropic to cut off Mythos 5 and Fable 5
summary: A Commerce letter asked Anthropic to restrict Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals; Anthropic shut off both for all customers; Mythos 5 was partially restored to US critical-infrastructure defenders on June 27.
significance: Interpretation: first de facto US government recall of a deployed commercial frontier model; model access became export-controlled.

title: EU Digital Omnibus delays AI Act high-risk obligations
summary: Parliament adopted the deal delaying Annex III high-risk obligations from Aug 2, 2026 to Dec 2, 2027 and Annex I to Aug 2, 2028.
significance: Interpretation: Europe shifted from rule-setting toward competitiveness, mirroring the US deregulatory turn.

title: LBNL update: data centers 4.7% of US power in 2024, ~11.8% by 2030
summary: LBNL's 2025 update projected data centers at 11.8% of US electricity by 2030 (range 9.5-15.3%); secondary reporting puts 2024 use at 192 TWh (4.7%).
significance: Interpretation: near-term load came in below some forecasts, but the decade outlook still implies a structural power build.

title: Bipartisan federal AI preemption discussion draft
summary: Reps. Obernolte and Trahan released a draft freezing state laws on AI development for three years; it stalled by September.
significance: Interpretation: legislative preemption remained unresolved, leaving a patchwork of state laws.

title: Claude Opus 5 launches the Claude 5 family
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 at $5/$25 per 1M tokens with 1M context, alongside Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 tiers.
significance: Interpretation: frontier list prices held flat while capability rose.

title: Nvidia Q2 FY2027: $89B data center quarter, $108B guide
summary: NVIDIA reported revenue ~$96.2B and data center $89.0B (+117% y/y), guided Q3 to $108B, and said Vera Rubin was ramping.
significance: Interpretation: AI hardware demand was still accelerating at the research cutoff.

title: Lab run-rates reach ~$65-70B (Anthropic, OpenAI)
summary: Anthropic's run-rate reportedly topped $65B by end-July 2026 (from ~$9B at end-2025); OpenAI's reportedly neared $70B in September.
significance: Interpretation: if accurate, AI model revenue grew fast enough to narrow Sequoia's '$600B question' gap, though run-rates are not audited revenue.

title: GPT-6 'Astra' rolls out with cyber guardrails
summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 Astra to business testers, with a cyber-guardrailed version for paid ChatGPT users; reported API price $10/$50 per 1M tokens.
significance: Interpretation: frontier list prices rose again for the newest tier, and cyber controls became a launch prerequisite.

title: Claude Opus 5.5 at lower price
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per 1M tokens, 20% below Opus 5 on list price (the source headline says 40% cheaper, possibly on effective cost).
significance: Interpretation: price competition at the frontier continued alongside capability gains.
